The description contains hedged or minimizing language that fails the strict no-negative-signal criterion:
- "many shoppers say the bands hold their elasticity over time" is a hedged, attributed claim. It qualifies the product's performance rather than stating a pure positive, and it draws on review content about elasticity.
- "grips gently" is a softened, qualified description of grip strength, which reads as a mild caveat.
- "Your hair stays put so you can focus on what matters" directly answers the reviewer complaint that the band "does tend to slip off slowly" and "did not stay on my weird shaped head." Addressing that same issue, even with a positive claim, counts under the criterion.
